target_customer: Mid-market finance teams and manufacturers running accounts payable on ERPs such as NetSuite, Epicor and SAP
problem: AP teams manually match invoices, code lines and chase approvals; Clerked agents automate intake, three way matching and vendor replies.
business_model: B2B SaaS AP automation; pricing not stated

founders.name: Evan Meyer
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, computer science and statistics
previous_startups: Mod AI (accounts payable automation, later renamed Clerked)
founders.background_notes: Also worked at several startups per YC page

founders.name: Sunjeet Chugh
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, computer science and statistics (on leave)
previous_startups: Mod AI, co-founded with Evan Meyer

technical_complexity.rationale: Invoice extraction, three way matching, GL coding and exception handling across 16 plus ERPs; standard engineering with heavy integration work.

defensibility.rationale: ERP integrations and policy configuration create some lock in, but AP automation is a crowded category with established vendors named on the Clerked site (Esker, Medius).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established AP vendors exist; no copying or acquisition event of Clerked found.

market_need_then: AP automation is a mature spend category; the Clerked site cites customers cutting invoice cycle time by 85 percent and approval time from one week to two hours (company claims).

rebrands.why: Not stated; exact date unknown. The Mod AI launch post is dated 2025-10-14 and YC now lists Clerked

brand_strength.rationale: Clerked is a clearer name than Mod AI for AP, but no press on the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Clerked, formerly Mod AI, sells AI agents for accounts payable to ERP based mid-market firms and lists named customers with cycle time claims. Funding is unreliable in aggregators and no outcome is public, so the company is simply early in a crowded AP category with strong incumbents.
notes: Aggregators conflict: CB Insights and VC Backed show 500K pre-seed from Y Combinator, a Caplight page shows 105.2M and a Series C, which is implausible and ignored. None recorded as a round. Competitor evidence was 2026 vendor comparison pages, so no dated competitors are listed. Rename date from Mod AI is unknown.
